As it stands this product is... not so good. I'm well-aware of the roguelike bad RNG nature of games, but you don't even often get rewards from bosses for your own playstyle. As in, the character you chose to play. Beyond relics and outfits there's also not much replayability here, a big part of roguelikes. And the souls-like difficulty of the game really relies on you getting fair RNG results, which you normally won't, so you ultimately waste time on bosses you can't beat because loot was stingy. Just all-around a game that needs mechanical reworks.

EDIT: I need to add some clarification. Do I think this game should be easy? No. I think it should be challenging but FAIR. Your effort is simply not enough for most players with how RNG does not play in your character's favor. Should RNG just be kind and forgiving? I don't necessarily think so, but RNG should offer things that benefit the character you play, not just.... no one in particular. Due to the overtuned nature of bosses, if you find yourself with poor RNG boons and items, you simply waste time trying to get better odds.  The sweats will say "get gud" or "go play an easier game" but I beat Elden Ring twice, and while I like the combat changes they've made to Nightreign, it needs work. Not to mention the network issues. Not saying this game is unplayable, but I'm saying From Software has never really been all that good at multiplayer experiences, and this is no exception.

This game is an objective failure of a rougelike and probably the worst one ive ever played. It has never defined itself as such, but such it is. Notice I said rougelike, and not rougelite. This is because there is no meta progression in this game, and anyone who has told you otherwise is either misinformed or lying. The only form of meta progression is cosmetics and 100% rng relics to equip that give like +1 to a stat or something. Someone could unequip them from your character and you wouldn't notice. All of the best relics are given to you through rewards and quest progression. It is a fruitless endeavor trying to roll for a good relic. You will not get it. There are a billion modifiers and only like 10 of them are good. All the rewards you get from beating a run are therefore useless, since the game hands you the best relics and no RNG reward you get will ever come close.

So no meta progression really, okay that can still be fine. What about the gameplay loop? I am going to make a bold statement and say that I have never seen a more bland rougelike in my life. One of the primary selling points of the genre is VARIETY. Each run being unique. This game has the least variety between runs ive ever seen in a rougelike by far. You do the same things every run, and the gameplay loop ends up being a checklist simulator. There is nothing that can happen that will really change how you play the game at any point. There is no cool loot to get, no interesting builds. Every item you get gives a random passive, 99% of which are incredibly boring flat stat increases that I honestly never feel in the first place. You can get a legendary weapon, but even they don't feel special. At no point do you ever get that overwhelming feeling of curating drops all run to have a build culminate and feel it gradually get more and more op that is a staple of the genre. There is no way to curate your RNG, you can get caster items all run if you are melee. You never feel op. You have zero control over your leveling. There is absolutely no room for any sort of customization mid run. 

This game is groundbreaking repetitive and has an astounding lack of content. Playtimes are heavily skewed by the fact that most people are going to be playing solo or with randoms ontop of the overall difficulty if you don't do everything the exact same way every run. There are no interesting choices to make mid run. You cant make a risk and go to the castle at level one. Level dictates everything. It doesn't matter how skilled you are, it will be impossible. The risk is instant death, and the reward is likely nothing. You get a boss drop where you pick between 3 buffs that are useless to you lol. All of this shoehorns you into playing a very very specific manner and trying anything else is punished heavily by the storm, time limits, level gated areas and fights, etc. These things make the game feel even smaller and incredibily frustrating. All fromsoft jank is 100 times worse when you are on a strict time limit. Platforming, hit detection, enemy AI is all cute until it ends a run. 

What about some other standard practices? An endless mode maybe? Why is every run forced to end? How about some sort of boss rush? Where is the replayability? Once you see all the nightlords there is no reason to play, the base gameplay loop simply doesn't offer a shred of completxity to keep players long term.

40 dollars for this game is robbery, they are spitting in your face. This is barely worth 20, and thats just going off the amount of content with nothing to say about the quality of said content. I would be more willing to forgive some of its sins with a lower price tag, but they are charging 40 dollars and they have a deluxe edition and a collectors edition for this thing. Pinning any critism on "muh B team" or "its just an experiment bro" is not going to work. If it is such an experimental thing that isnt made by fromsofts best then why charge so much? Why set that expectation of quality? Is this the quality of fromsofts work if miyazaki isn't watching every move? 

All of this incredibly baffling considering that this is the most flagrant and blatant reuse of assets I have ever seen. It takes genuine balls to do this, if I didn't know better and was shown this I would have thought it was just a free high effort elden ring mod. I am not kidding when I say that this game is only about 5% nightreign exclusive content. 

Safe to say their little experiment was a massive success financially and an absolute disaster of game design that you don't get to see often. Even the reddit FS diehard glazers can't help but notice these things. This isn't even mentioning all of the problems that are known like voice chat, duos, no crossplay, etc. 

This game only really holds a shred of fun after a few hours if you have any friends to play with, but if the bar is low enough to be fun to play with friends then we have truly lost the plot.

From soft game is good, any surprise there? not really. Now here for some advice. You don't have to have a weapon in your hand to receive it's passive unless it has a hand symbol on it. You don't have to do the nightlords in order but you can if you want to. You can check the scaling of any character in the visual codex next to the jar merchant. Remembrance quests are very useful as they give relics specifically designed for that character. If in a party, only the hosts remembrance quest can be done. Now for some character specific advice.
Guardian (my current main): you will survive almost anything as long as you use your "special blocking" (hold block and then dodge to activate). Use your ult to revive people or to cover someones risky play, if you hold the ult button you will grant invincibility to yourself and nearby allies (and with the right relics they'll heal).
Revenant (my backup main): You can keep your summons alive a lot longer if you cycle between them when the current one is low on hp. You don't have much hp so stay a decent ways back, similar to guardian your ult can instantly revive anyone so use it for similar purposes as guardian's ult.
Recluse (my other backup main): High damage, high range, high versatility but low hp. Your ability regains fp for you and absorbs a "charge" of the last elemental damage dealt (holy, lightning, magic, fire) to that enemy, once 3 "charges" have been absorbed you can use your actual abilities (there are a lot). Remember these for use in game: Lightning + holy = auto parry, Fire + holy = health buff for allies and health debuff for enemies, Magic + Lightning = moonveil skill (kinda), Fire + Lightning + Holy = zeus, Magic = orbs the follow enemies and attack every few seconds.
Wylder (my old main): You are a literal speed demon. Ever played Doom: eternal? your ability is the meathook on the super shotgun. For a little extra distance out of your ability, jump at the end of the animation and you'll go flying. Your ult has 3 "settings": regular tap will do a small explosion in front of you and launches you back, jumping tap is almost identical but can be used at the end of that speed trick, charging will do a massive close range explosion with i want to say about double damge but half the range and no knockback for you.
Dutchess (Have played her now but nothing to change about what I said really): Haven't played this one yet so take this with a grain of salt. Your ability is the strongest in the whole game but your ult is the most situational (being polite). Your ability will deal all the damage dealt within the last few seconds again (with a small decrease), 12 second cooldown as well. Your ult is only really useful for a clutch revive as it turns you and nearby allies invisible for about 10 seconds, good if your the last one standing but almost pointless anywhere else.
Executor: Your skill is a toggle for an unstoppable defensive ability as long as you've got good timing. Blocking just before an enemy attacks with your ability active will deflect (parry) the attack, this deflect counts as guarding for passives in game. To clarify, your ability can parry ANYTHING if it deals damage (you'll still get status effects).
Ironeye: As an ironeye you want to stay out of enemy range but not so far out that your arrows arrive in 4-5 buissness days. Your ability is a dash (with i-frames) that marks enemies caught in it's path, enemies with this mark take 10% extra damage and after a certain amount of damage is dealt will do an extra huge chunk of damage. You ult has a good amount of range (shocker) and has a decent amount of aoe and pierces enemies so you can use it to take out a horde very quickly.
Raider: Just don't play this one
Raider (after playing a bit more of him (He's now one of my mains :) )): As Raider, your main job is to sit at the frontline taking damage and staggering any enemies out of an attack that could really hurt. This means you need to be looking out for passives like "Taking damage improves damage negation" and any passive that just flat out improves any form of damage negation. Your ability needs to build up "charge", this charge builds by taking damage, once it is fully charged it will glow (kinda, it will have a blue outline). The reason I said just don't play him previously is that he relies on getting certain passives or the right relics, but once you get those passives or those relics he becomes one of the best characters in the entire game. Once fully charged his ability feels like an ult and hits like an ult and will cancel most boss's attacks, your attacks are slow as hell but hit harder than the boss you're fighting. 
I hope this helps, have a good day

Well, for the price, you'll get your money's worth... and it's fine... but I'm one achievement off all achieves and have put over 80 hours into the game and I can very confidently say;

It's not very fun. I don't actually have FUN while playing. Even when we're winning and on a win streak of like 3-5+ matches in a row, it's just not really fun. It's basically something to do... it feels like playing LoL in that way. Where it's not fun and you hate the people you get stuck playing with that aren't your IRL friends you're in voice with.

The characters are extremely basic and lack meaningful customizability for their gameplay. The relics are overwhelmingly uninteresting AND bad. There are very few relic buffs that are worth caring about, outside of the character specific ones (which there should be like 2-4x of that drastically change the way the character can be played).

The Nightlords are, mostly, just poorly thought out trash that spam massive AoE attacks or run 10,000 miles back and forth across the area so that you cannot hit them, as a replacement for a well designed fight. I wouldn't go so far as to say they're bad bosses, just not well designed or thought out because the combat in FromSoft's Souls games and Elden Ring is not very well designed to be interesting or engaging. So with such limited and boring combat, you can't really make fun bosses, just passable bosses that you instead focus on making LOOK cool and aiming for spectacle over substance. Again, not bad, just... basic Souls bosses but made worse than normal by them not knowing how to make a boss that is intended to be fought by more than a single person.

The combat is helped with the character's abilities, but that zero customization for their gameplay lingers grossly at all times; with them being designed to punish you for not playing within certain parameters on top.

The buffs you gain from killing bosses are limited and lame in the same way the relic buffs are, mostly instead being a place to try to get weapons, but due to there being no "default" choice when the 7th boss in a row drops nothing useful for you, it ends up feeling VERY bad after several runs in a row where you simply don't get anything you could meaningfully use. I've lost count of how often I will go entire runs without ever seeing a single large shield as Guardian, even when my two friends are also keeping an eye out for me. There should ALWAYS be an option to just take more ruins instead of any of the worthless options, or some other default choice. Even just consumables or something based on what the boss was, like 2 greases of the boss' element or boulases for their main status effect so you can get stacking those passive buffs from them up to +9.

The fact that there is no Duo queue is also pure, absolute, cancer. Randos in this game are HORRIBLE at the game about 80% of the time. It's nice when you get someone that is on your level, or even those rarer times when you get someone very good... but when our third isn't available, having to suffer the morons that play this game can be rough.

Also add the normal amount of FromSoft ineptitude and lack of common sense with NEVER giving appropriate tooltips or information about stats and how things work, and you end up frustrated on a consistent basis over not being sure HOW some of the passives function. FromSoft have always sucked at actually being good at making games, it's a weird thing about them... they're like idiot savants or something. Thankfully the playerbase rips the games apart and does their job for them eventually.

It's worth the money and you will get your playtime out of it... but it's not fun, it's just a thing to do with some friends.

At first I fell for the "this game sucks, there's no way to communicate with your teammates" slander than was going around. I really hope FS support this game for the foreseeable future. There are tons of additional items, weapons, arts, spells, incantations, enemies, bosses, etc. they can add from the SotE DLC, let alone from the Dark Souls games. Please increase the probability of shifting earth events, walking mausoleums, and certain night bosses. I have 50+ hours, and I have never fought the smelter demon or seen a mausoleum. I have not seen a crater event since the initial scripted one. Who knows what else I've never seen....

I think my only criticism at this point is that there should be crossplay between all consoles and PC. This isn't a competitive FPS where aim is important. Make us one big community! Also, there are still some frame drops here and there depending on the amount of effects happening simultaneously. Besides that, this game is a better monster hunter than Monster Hunter Wilds.
